source.title: Constructing Interpretable Features from Compositional Neuron Groups
source.authors: O. Shafran; Atticus Geiger; Mor Geva

record.file_problem: The text is substantially complete; minor PDF/OCR artifacts occur in equations and formatting.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures shared neuron structure across related MLP features and causally intervenes on neuron groups, providing a different-method test relevant to the related-jobs refinement in V6. It does not measure individual-neuron polysemanticity or its prevalence.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior claims that neurons can participate in multiple concepts, but cited findings are not rows. Its concept-detection and steering benchmark results compare feature-discovery methods; they do not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so those results are omitted. The weekday neuron-overlap and group-intervention results bear on V6; the broader parent-child feature results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper takes as given that individual neurons encode multiple concepts, citing Olah et al. 2020 among others, and uses this to motivate decomposing MLP activations with SNMF. Most of its results score its own method against SAEs and DiffMeans on detection and steering. The weekday and hierarchy analyses measure how groups of neurons are shared across semantically related SNMF features. No result measures whether, or how often, individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. None re-examines a canonical polysemantic neuron, varies architecture or capacity, or varies the measurement. So no version of the claim is tested; the neuron-sharing findings are a related construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that SNMF features match SAEs on concept detection and beat SAEs and DiffMeans on steering. They add that neuron composition explains why the same neurons contribute to multiple features, and that SAE feature splitting may reflect this composition rather than being an SAE artifact.
record.recipe_differences: The study decomposes language-model MLP activations with SNMF and intervenes on neuron groups; it does not reproduce the visual-neuron analysis or method of the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that which concepts and effects are examined depends on the selected features, layers, and datasets; no sensitivity analysis of individual-neuron polysemanticity is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantically related SNMF features (weekdays) share a core set of MLP neurons and differ by exclusive neurons. Amplifying the core raises all weekday logits; amplifying a day's exclusive neurons mostly promotes that day and suppresses the others (GPT-2 Large).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neurons are reused compositionally across semantically related features, with shared cores encoding the general concept and exclusive neurons the specific one.

fits_no_version.finding: In recursive SNMF hierarchies, parent features' promoted tokens cover about 0.37–0.47 of their children's, versus 0.00–0.05 for random pairing. Children stay diverse (diversity 0.99).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hierarchical MLP feature groups can have causal effects that cover multiple diverse child-feature effects.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), as stated in the supplied metadata; the paper text also identifies an arXiv version.
record.problems: The individual-neuron claim is not directly evaluated: the principal overlap and causal evidence concerns neuron groups/features and a weekday example. The recursive hierarchy analysis uses generated datasets and selected examples; the paper notes that the hierarchy examples are manually selected. Evaluation relies on LLM judges, with a human agreement check on 50 examples (Spearman ρ = 0.8, p < 10−4).
record.rows_left_out: Concept-detection and concept-steering benchmark results were not extracted because they assess learned feature descriptions or steering performance, not individual-neuron polysemanticity. Other recursive feature-hierarchy examples are qualitative and do not independently measure the claim.

untested.parts: Vision models and InceptionV1 neurons; not studied.
Share of individual MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and how it varies by layer.
Superposition or capacity as the cause of polysemanticity.
Dependence of polysemanticity on activation function, architecture or regularization.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons are misread generalizations. Neuron sharing is shown only between related SNMF features, with no analysis of single-neuron responses.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link is overstated. Sharing neurons across related features is not evidence that canonical polysemantic neurons are misread, because no individual neuron's response profile is examined. The paper's remark that a neuron may participate in multiple concepts is an inference from its framework, not a measurement.

versions.untested_parts: Image classifiers, InceptionV1, and visual neuron responses.
The share of individual transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and variation in that share across layers.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than available neurons or by capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity from initialization, regularization, or training noise when capacity is sufficient.
Changes in individual-neuron polysemanticity across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, including SoLU and modern convnets, and associated performance costs.

The study examines shared and specific neuron groups for weekday concepts, not canonical individual polysemantic neurons. It does not establish how often unrelated mixtures are reinterpretable as one job or related offshoots.
Sensitivity of polysemanticity judgments to activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Counted overlaps among top-activating neurons in MLP features; the first seven features represent weekdays and other features were randomly sampled.

conditions.value: weekday features versus other sampled MLP features

rows.measure: Number of overlapping top-activating neurons between feature pairs
rows.value: Text reports higher shared counts among weekday features, with little overlap with the remaining sampled features; figure provides the heatmap.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a shared core for weekday features plus additional neurons refining the representation. This is feature-level overlap, not a test of individual-neuron responses to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Shows overlap of top neurons between SNMF features (shared core for related weekday features). It does not show individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs or polysemantic neurons reinterpreted as one job, so it does not bear on V6. The model for Fig. 5 is not stated; it is likely GPT-2 (Fig. 4 uses GPT-2 Small, Table 2 uses GPT-2 Large). There is no numeric baseline beyond comparison with randomly sampled features.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Large
rows.operation_detail: Amplified the neuron base shared across weekday MLP features and measured changes in weekday-token logits.

conditions.value: base neurons shared across all weekday MLP features

rows.measure: Change in logits for Monday through Sunday tokens
rows.baseline: Non-intervened output logits; baseline values not stated
rows.value: Monday 5.8; Tuesday 5.7; Wednesday 5.4; Thursday 5.8; Friday 6.0; Saturday 5.4; Sunday 4.7
rows.note: The paper says amplifying the shared base promotes all weekday tokens, consistent with a general weekday-related contribution.
rows.check: Causal effect of amplifying a group of shared neurons on weekday logits. This is a neuron-group or feature effect, not an individual neuron's polysemanticity; it does not bear on V6.

reader_labels.condition: Weekday neuron-group example in GPT-2 Large
reader_labels.reason: Shared weekday neurons promote all weekday tokens, while exclusive groups generally promote their corresponding day and suppress others, consistent with shared and related specific jobs rather than unrelated mixtures at the group level (r2–r9).
